Q: Vlookup function syntax between two sheets A:

In the event your spreadsheet locale uses commas , as decimal separators, as in € 1,50, you will have to use semicolons ; as formula argument separators. In other words, replace all the commas in the formula with semicolons. See Set a spreadsheet’s location & calculation settings and Syntax differences in formulas by Ben Collins for more info.

To refer to another sheet, use this syntax:

=vlookup(A2; 'The name of the other sheet'!A2:B; 2; false)

A common issue with cross-sheet references is with leading or trailing spaces in the sheet name. Double-click the tab of the other sheet in the tab bar at the bottom of the window and remove superfluous spaces, if any.

You can find additional info on vlookup() syntax details at the vlookup() help page.

If the problem is with something else, show your work.

Q: Can't execute script in GitLab CI/CD A:

The issue is in your release_bin script. The glob pattern "./bin/*" is quoted, which prevents bash from expanding it. Instead of iterating through files, you're literally assigning the string "./bin/*" to your loop variable.

Change this line in release_bin:

for f in "./bin/*"

To this (remove the quotes):

for f in ./bin/*

Q: DBT BigQuery error: Quota exceeded: Your table exceeded quota for imports or query appends per table A:

If you are running dbt incremental models in BigQuery and hitting "Quota exceeded" errors on job limits, you may be running into a known bug in BigQuery’s handling of partitioned tables.

When dbt performs an incremental merge, it executes a CREATE OR REPLACE statement to build a temporary table. BigQuery currently misinterprets these operations: it counts every partition in the temporary table as an individual query job.

For example, if your staging data contains 25 partitions, BigQuery treats that single CREATE statement as 25 distinct query jobs. If you run your dbt models frequently (e.g., every 15 minutes), these jobs accumulate rapidly, quickly exhausting your daily BigQuery job quota. In my case, I run every 15 minutes and have 25 partitions, so it hit this quota limit (also check this: https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/quotas#standard_tables)

The Workaround

Google has confirmed this is a bug they are working to resolve, but until a fix is deployed, you can bypass this by ensuring your temporary table names are always unique to prevent collisions and job-queuing issues.

You can achieve this by overriding the make_temp_relation macro to append the dbt invocation_id to the table name:

SQL

-- Put this in your macros/override_temp_relation.sql
{% macro make_temp_relation(base_relation, suffix='__dbt_tmp') %}
  {%- set suffix_with_invocation_id = suffix ~ '__' ~ invocation_id -%}
  {{ return(adapter.dispatch('make_temp_relation', 'dbt')(base_relation, suffix_with_invocation_id)) }}
{% endmacro %}

By appending the invocation_id, each incremental run generates a unique temporary table. This prevents BigQuery from bundling or miscounting these operations against your job quota.
